spawning.answer: Look around active creaking hearts in pale gardens at night. A heart can also be activated outside that biome in the Overworld with correctly aligned pale oak blocks.

drops.answer: Creakings do not drop items or experience on death. Hitting a heart-linked creaking can cause resin clumps to appear on nearby pale-oak logs; resin is not ordinary kill loot.

combat.answer: A heart-linked creaking is protected by its heart. Look at it to stop its movement, then locate and break the linked creaking heart. Simply attacking the protected mob does not defeat it.

interactions.answer: A creaking cannot move while an eligible player is looking at it. Hitting it can reveal its linked heart through particles and generate resin near that heart.

taming.answer: Creaking cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Creaking cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

health.answer: A heart-linked creaking is protected by its creaking heart. Its tiny internal health value does not make it a normal one-hit enemy; break the linked heart to defeat it.

fire.answer: A creaking linked to a creaking heart is protected and cannot be defeated like an ordinary flammable mob. Its heart-linked state matters; remove the linked heart.

sunlight.answer: Heart-linked creakings are active at night and disappear when the heart becomes inactive in the day. This is a heart/day-cycle rule, not ordinary zombie-style sun burning.

vibrations.answer: A heart-linked creaking can be stopped by an eligible player looking at it. Hitting it can reveal the linked heart with particles; a warden’s vibration rules are a different mechanic.

variants.answer: Naturally heart-linked creakings depend on a creaking heart. A command-created creaking can behave differently from one linked to a heart.

spawn_conditions.answer: At night in the Overworld, an activated creaking heart needs pale oak blocks on opposite sides along its own axis and a valid nearby spawning space. The heart-linked creaking differs from a command-created one; an ordinary dark platform alone does not produce it.

experience.answer: It gives no experience when killed. Item drops and rewards from other interactions are separate.

identity.answer: A creaking is a hostile tree-like mob linked to a creaking heart. It moves when players are not looking at it. Deal with the linked heart rather than relying on ordinary attacks against the mob.

behavior.answer: A creaking is a hostile tree-like mob linked to a creaking heart. It moves when players are not looking at it. Deal with the linked heart rather than relying on ordinary attacks against the mob.

spawning.answer: Creepers naturally spawn in dark Overworld areas, excluding mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains in Bedrock.

drops.answer: A normal creeper can drop 0–2 gunpowder when it dies; Looting can increase that amount. If a skeleton, stray or bogged kills it, it can drop a music disc. If another charged creeper kills it, it can drop a creeper head.

combat.answer: Creepers approach players and explode at close range. Back away before the fuse finishes and use distance or solid cover. Charged creepers have stronger explosions; damage depends on distance, difficulty and protection.

interactions.answer: Lightning can turn a normal creeper into a charged creeper. A Channeling trident can help create the required lightning under suitable weather conditions. Cats and ocelots scare creepers.

variants.answer: Creepers have ordinary and charged forms. Lightning creates the charged form; its stronger explosion can enable mob-head drops from eligible victims.

taming.answer: Creeper cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Creeper cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

lightning.answer: Lightning turns a creeper into a charged creeper. A suitable Channeling-trident hit during a thunderstorm can create the required lightning.

anger.answer: A creeper approaches a target and starts its fuse at close range. Cats and ocelots scare it, but do not make every possible situation safe.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

spawn_conditions.answer: For ordinary natural spawning, check darkness, a suitable solid surface, space, enabled mob spawning and a difficulty above Peaceful. Bedrock excludes mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains. Lighting can prevent spawning; it does not remove an existing creeper.

experience.answer: It gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: A creeper is a hostile mob that approaches players and explodes. Its explosion can damage you and nearby blocks. Keep your distance; cats and ocelots help deter it.

behavior.answer: A creeper is a hostile mob that approaches players and explodes. Its explosion can damage you and nearby blocks. Keep your distance; cats and ocelots help deter it.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

identity.answer: A charged creeper is the lightning-charged form with a stronger explosion.

spawning.answer: Lightning turns an ordinary creeper into a charged creeper. A suitable Channeling-trident strike can produce the required lightning during a thunderstorm.

combat.answer: Keep distance and use cover. A charged creeper’s explosion is stronger than an ordinary creeper’s.

interactions.answer: Cushions are placeable seats. Use one to sit on it. They need a supporting surface and can break when that support is removed.

drops.answer: A cushion drops its own item when broken. It is a placeable seat, not a creature that provides animal loot.

identity.answer: A cushion is a seat-like decorative entity. Place and interact with it as a seat in compatible builds.

behavior.answer: A cushion is a seat-like decorative entity. Place and interact with it as a seat in compatible builds.

spawning.answer: Look in ocean water between Y=50 and Y=64, excluding cold and frozen oceans.

drops.answer: Adult dolphins can drop raw cod, or cooked cod if killed while burning. Baby dolphins do not give item or experience drops.

breeding.answer: Dolphins cannot be bred by players; baby dolphins come from natural spawning.

taming.answer: Dolphins cannot be tamed. Feeding fish is a treasure-guidance interaction, not ownership.

interactions.answer: Feed raw cod or salmon to have a dolphin lead toward a nearby shipwreck or ocean ruins. It does not guarantee treasure remains there. Bedrock swimming boosts are not displayed as the Java Dolphin’s Grace status effect.

combat.answer: Adult dolphins can retaliate when attacked, and nearby dolphins may join the fight. Baby dolphins are passive. Feeding fish and attacking a dolphin are different interactions.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: Dolphins need both water and access to air. They surface to breathe and can drown if kept submerged without an air supply.

land.answer: Dolphins also dry out on land. An enclosure must provide water and access to air, rather than trapping one underwater.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Dolphins have baby and adult stages. Babies can spawn naturally; feeding two dolphins does not breed a baby.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural dolphins need an eligible ocean biome and Y=50–64. A river, cold ocean or frozen ocean is not the same habitat. Breeding dolphins with fish does not create new dolphins.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

treasure.answer: Feed a dolphin raw fish such as raw cod or raw salmon, then follow it toward a nearby shipwreck or ocean ruin. Feeding does not tame it, make it rideable or guarantee that the structure contains untouched loot.

speed.answer: Sprint-swimming near a dolphin gives a swimming speed boost. In Bedrock this is not displayed as a Dolphin’s Grace status effect. It does not give you underwater breathing, so still watch your air.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

identity.answer: A dolphin is a neutral aquatic mammal found in oceans. Swimming nearby can help with movement in water, and feeding it raw fish can help guide you toward certain underwater loot locations. It needs air as well as water.

behavior.answer: A dolphin is a neutral aquatic mammal found in oceans. Swimming nearby can help with movement in water, and feeding it raw fish can help guide you toward certain underwater loot locations. It needs air as well as water.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

spawning.answer: Look for donkeys in plains, meadows and savannas.

health.answer: A donkey’s maximum health can range from 15 to 30 health points; individual animals have different attributes.

drops.answer: Adult donkeys can drop leather. Any equipped saddle, attached chest and chest contents also drop. Babies have no normal item or experience drops.

taming.answer: Repeatedly mount an adult donkey until it accepts you and shows hearts. Once tamed, equip a saddle to control it.

breeding.answer: Feed golden apples or golden carrots to two tamed adult donkeys. A tamed donkey and tamed horse can instead produce a mule; mules cannot breed.

transport.answer: A tamed, saddled donkey can be ridden. Attach a chest to give it storage. It does not use horse armor.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

storage.answer: A tamed donkey or mule can be equipped with a chest to carry inventory. Its storage chest and riding saddle are separate pieces of equipment.

equipment.answer: Use a saddle on the tamed animal to control riding, and optionally a chest for storage. It does not use ordinary horse armor.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Donkeys have baby and adult stages. A mule is the offspring of a horse and a donkey, not a donkey coat variant.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural Bedrock donkeys occur in plains, meadows and savannas. A meadow is valid even though it is not an ordinary cow habitat. Breeding requires existing compatible animals; it is separate from waiting for wild donkeys.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

equipment_drops.answer: An equipped donkey drops its saddle, attached chest and chest contents when killed. These are carried items, not extra guaranteed contents generated by Looting.

identity.answer: A donkey is a tameable riding animal. Equip it with a saddle to ride and a chest to carry supplies. It can breed with a horse to produce a mule.

behavior.answer: A donkey is a tameable riding animal. Equip it with a saddle to ride and a chest to carry supplies. It can breed with a horse to produce a mule.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Equip it with a saddle to ride and a chest to carry supplies. It can breed with a horse to produce a mule.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

spawning.answer: The Ender Dragon fires dragon fireballs during its attacks.

combat.answer: A dragon fireball creates a damaging area on impact. Move out of the lingering breath cloud rather than standing in it.

interactions.answer: Use glass bottles on the dragon’s breath cloud to collect dragon’s breath.

identity.answer: A dragon fireball is a projectile fired by the Ender Dragon. It creates a dangerous effect cloud, so move away from the impact area.

behavior.answer: A dragon fireball is a projectile fired by the Ender Dragon. It creates a dangerous effect cloud, so move away from the impact area.

spawning.answer: Look in oceans, rivers and dripstone-cave water. Some ocean ruins generate drowned. Ordinary zombies can also convert after prolonged submersion.

drops.answer: Drowned can drop rotten flesh and, under the appropriate player-kill conditions, a copper ingot. A drowned carrying a trident or fishing rod has a separate chance to drop that item; one carrying a nautilus shell drops the shell. Not every drowned carries a trident.

combat.answer: Some drowned throw tridents, while others attack up close. They are undead, so Smite is useful. Water and daylight affect their behavior; do not assume every drowned will pursue you onto dry land.

interactions.answer: Ordinary zombies can convert to drowned after remaining submerged. Drowned can spawn holding different equipment, which changes both their attacks and their possible drops.

taming.answer: Drowned cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Drowned cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

growth.answer: Baby undead of this kind do not normally grow into adults while they remain undead. A cured baby zombie villager can later grow as a living villager.

variants.answer: Drowned can be babies or adults, and their held equipment can differ. A trident is equipment, not a separate species.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural spawning needs water with no emitted block light and sky light 7 or less. Bedrock uses surface spawning checks, not Java’s universal below-Y=58 rule. Rivers and dripstone caves have higher rates than oceans. Zombie conversion and ocean-ruin generation are separate sources.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points for an adult or 12 for a baby after an eligible player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add experience; items picked up later are a separate category.

experience_baby.answer: The base baby reward is 12 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add more; this is different from ordinary baby animals giving no experience.

equipment_drops.answer: In Bedrock, its naturally held trident or fishing rod has a 25% drop chance after a player or tamed-wolf kill, plus one percentage point per Looting level, up to 28% with Looting III. The creature must actually hold or wear that item; picked-up equipment is separate.

identity.answer: A drowned is an underwater zombie that can also move on land. Watch for trident-wielding drowned during water travel. Its available equipment and drops vary.

behavior.answer: A drowned is an underwater zombie that can also move on land. Watch for trident-wielding drowned during water travel. Its available equipment and drops vary.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

sunlight.answer: It can burn in direct sunlight when unprotected. Shade, water and applicable armor protection can prevent that; sunlight protection does not make it immune to lava.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It can also breathe air.

spawning.answer: Throw an egg item or dispense it to create an egg projectile.

interactions.answer: A thrown egg can hatch chicks on impact, but hatching is not guaranteed. It is different from placing a turtle or sniffer egg block.

hatching.answer: A thrown chicken egg can hatch chicks on impact, but it is not guaranteed. Chicken eggs are thrown rather than placed as incubating turtle/sniffer egg blocks.

identity.answer: An egg is an item laid by chickens that can also be thrown as a projectile. Use it in food recipes or throw it for a chance of hatching a chicken.

behavior.answer: An egg is an item laid by chickens that can also be thrown as a projectile. Use it in food recipes or throw it for a chance of hatching a chicken.

spawning.answer: Each ocean monument generates three elder guardians: one in the top room and one in each wing. They do not naturally respawn.

drops.answer: Elder guardians can drop prismarine materials, wet sponge under the required kill conditions, and a chance of a Tide armor trim smithing template. Their drops are separate from regular guardians.

combat.answer: Elder guardians use a charging beam and inflict Mining Fatigue on nearby players. Bring underwater breathing and a plan for Mining Fatigue; breaking line of sight can interrupt beam attacks.

taming.answer: Elder guardian cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Elder guardian cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: An elder guardian is a separate mob from a guardian. A normal guardian does not grow into an elder guardian.

spawn_conditions.answer: Elder guardians generate with the monument, not through a repeatable dark-water spawning cycle. Once the three are gone, waiting or rebuilding monument blocks will not naturally replace them.

experience.answer: It gives 10 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: An elder guardian is a large hostile aquatic mob found in ocean monuments. It uses a beam attack and can inflict Mining Fatigue, making monument exploration harder.

behavior.answer: An elder guardian is a large hostile aquatic mob found in ocean monuments. It uses a beam attack and can inflict Mining Fatigue, making monument exploration harder.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 80 health points (40 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: End crystals generate on the End’s obsidian pillars. Players can also place crystal items on obsidian or bedrock under suitable space conditions.

interactions.answer: End crystals heal the Ender Dragon and explode when destroyed. Four correctly placed around the exit portal can restart the dragon fight.

combat.answer: Keep your distance when destroying an End crystal: its explosion can cause severe damage and destroy nearby blocks.

identity.answer: An End crystal is an explosive crystal that can heal the Ender Dragon. It is used in the dragon-respawning arrangement. Breaking or attacking it causes a dangerous explosion.

behavior.answer: An End crystal is an explosive crystal that can heal the Ender Dragon. It is used in the dragon-respawning arrangement. Breaking or attacking it causes a dangerous explosion.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

spawning.answer: The ender dragon is the boss on the End’s central island. It appears with the initial dragon fight and can later be resummoned.

construction.answer: To resummon the dragon, place four End crystals around the End exit portal, one centered on each side. Stand clear during the crystal and tower-regeneration sequence.

drops.answer: The first dragon defeat gives a large amount of experience, opens the exit portal and produces the dragon egg at the portal. Later defeats give less experience. Dragon breath is collected with glass bottles during the fight, not from its death loot.

combat.answer: Destroy the healing End crystals, avoid the breath clouds and attack the dragon’s vulnerable head when an opening appears. Beds and other explosions are dangerous tactics and can kill you too.

taming.answer: Ender dragon cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Ender dragon cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

variants.answer: The Ender Dragon has different fight phases and can be resummoned. Those phases are not baby or coat variants.

spawn_conditions.answer: The first dragon is associated with entering the End. To resummon it after defeat, use four End crystals, one at the center of each side of the exit portal. A dark platform or a random crystal arrangement away from that portal does not resummon it.

experience.answer: The first defeated Ender Dragon gives 12,000 experience points. A resummoned dragon gives 500, not another 12,000. Experience points are not the same as player levels.

identity.answer: The Ender Dragon is a flying boss associated with the End's central island. It attacks players and can heal from End crystals. Defeating it opens important progression routes in the End.

behavior.answer: The Ender Dragon is a flying boss associated with the End's central island. It attacks players and can heal from End crystals. Defeating it opens important progression routes in the End.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 200 health points (100 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

spawning.answer: Throw an ender pearl or launch one from a dispenser to create its projectile.

interactions.answer: A player-thrown ender pearl teleports its thrower when it lands and normally causes teleportation damage. It can also create an endermite. Avoid throwing into unsafe terrain.

identity.answer: An ender pearl is a throwable teleportation item. Throw it to teleport to its landing location, usually taking teleportation damage. It is also used to craft eyes of ender.

behavior.answer: An ender pearl is a throwable teleportation item. Throw it to teleport to its landing location, usually taking teleportation damage. It is also used to craft eyes of ender.

spawning.answer: Endermen occur in the Overworld, Nether and End. Warped forests are especially useful in the Nether, and endermen are common in the End.

drops.answer: An enderman can drop 0–1 ender pearls, with Looting increasing applicable drops. It also drops the block it was carrying.

combat.answer: Looking directly at an enderman or attacking it can provoke it. It teleports and avoids many projectiles. Water hurts it, and a low shelter can help keep its tall body away.

interactions.answer: A carved pumpkin worn on your head prevents normal eye-contact provocation. Endermen can pick up and place certain blocks; they cannot move every block type.

taming.answer: Enderman cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Enderman cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

water.answer: Water damages endermen and can make them teleport away. They do not behave like ordinary swimming farm animals.

rain.answer: Rain can hurt exposed endermen. They seek shelter or teleport; being in a rainy biome is not a safe way to keep one in place.

teleportation.answer: Endermen can teleport to suitable nearby locations, especially when threatened. They cannot teleport to every block or through every environmental restriction.

anger.answer: Looking at an enderman’s face or attacking it can make it hostile. Wearing a carved pumpkin prevents the usual eye-contact provocation, but does not make attacking one safe.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight does not burn an enderman like a zombie, but bright conditions affect its behavior and it may teleport to shade. Rain and water can hurt it.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: An enderman may be calm, angry or carrying a block. These are behavior states rather than different breeds.

spawn_conditions.answer: Endermen need a suitable solid surface and three empty blocks above. They need darkness in the Overworld and End, or light 7 or less in the Nether. Bedrock Overworld exclusions include mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains.

experience.answer: It gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: An enderman is a tall neutral mob that can teleport and move certain blocks. It becomes hostile when provoked, including by looking into its eyes under suitable conditions. Water is dangerous to it.

behavior.answer: An enderman is a tall neutral mob that can teleport and move certain blocks. It becomes hostile when provoked, including by looking into its eyes under suitable conditions. Water is dangerous to it.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 40 health points (20 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: An endermite can appear when a player’s thrown ender pearl lands. In Bedrock it appears at the pearl’s landing site.

drops.answer: Endermites do not have a normal item drop; a player or tamed-wolf kill gives experience.

interactions.answer: Endermites normally disappear after about two minutes even inside vehicles. A name tag can prevent that timed disappearance.

taming.answer: Endermite cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Endermite cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: An endermite is its own small mob, not a baby enderman.

spawn_conditions.answer: A player-thrown ender pearl has a 5% chance to produce an endermite when it lands. A dark platform does not naturally generate them. Endermites disappear after about two minutes unless named with a name tag.

experience.answer: It gives 3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: An endermite is a small hostile creature that can appear after ender-pearl use. It attacks at close range and can attract the attention of endermen under the right conditions.

behavior.answer: An endermite is a small hostile creature that can appear after ender-pearl use. It attacks at close range and can attract the attention of endermen under the right conditions.

combat.answer: It is a hostile mob and can attack players. It attacks at close range and can attract the attention of endermen under the right conditions.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 8 health points (4 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Evokers generate in particular woodland-mansion rooms and appear during suitable raid waves. Mansion evokers do not respawn naturally.

drops.answer: An evoker drops a totem of undying and can drop emeralds. Raid-captain equipment and ominous bottles have their own conditions. In Bedrock, an evoker gives experience regardless of how it dies.

combat.answer: Evokers summon vexes and fang attacks. Their spells can threaten you from beyond ordinary melee reach; interrupt the fight quickly and watch for summoned vexes.

interactions.answer: An evoker can change a nearby blue sheep to red under the applicable mob-griefing conditions. A totem it drops works only when held in a hand when lethal damage occurs.

taming.answer: Evocation illager cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Evocation illager cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: An evoker encountered in a mansion or a raid is the same kind of illager. Summoned vexes are separate mobs.

spawn_conditions.answer: Mansion evokers generate once in particular upper-floor rooms and do not refill after being killed. Another source is a raid on Normal or Hard, starting at wave five. An Easy raid or a cleared mansion is not a repeatable evoker-spawning area.

experience.answer: In Bedrock an evoker gives 10 experience points regardless of how it dies. This differs from the usual player-kill requirement for many mobs.

identity.answer: An evoker is a spellcasting hostile illager. It summons vexes and magical fangs. It can drop a totem of undying when defeated.

behavior.answer: An evoker is a spellcasting hostile illager. It summons vexes and magical fangs. It can drop a totem of undying when defeated.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 24 health points (12 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Using an eye of ender in the Overworld launches the flying eye entity toward a stronghold.

interactions.answer: Follow the eye’s direction to locate a stronghold. It can drop back as an item or shatter, so carry spare eyes. This is separate from putting eyes into End portal frames.

identity.answer: A thrown eye of ender is a moving entity that points toward a stronghold. Follow its direction to search for a stronghold, collecting it again if it survives the throw.

behavior.answer: A thrown eye of ender is a moving entity that points toward a stronghold. Follow its direction to search for a stronghold, collecting it again if it survives the throw.

spawning.answer: Ghasts fire large fireballs. Fire charges launched by dispensers instead create small fireballs.

combat.answer: A ghast fireball explodes on impact and can be deflected back by a well-timed attack.

identity.answer: A large fireball is an explosive projectile commonly fired by ghasts. Avoid its impact or deflect it with a well-timed attack.

behavior.answer: A large fireball is an explosive projectile commonly fired by ghasts. Avoid its impact or deflect it with a well-timed attack.

spawning.answer: Using a firework rocket launches its entity. Rockets can also be launched from dispensers or crossbows.

interactions.answer: Firework rockets can boost a player gliding with elytra. Rockets containing firework stars explode and can hurt the user; use rockets without stars for safer boosting.

identity.answer: A firework rocket is a launched firework entity. It can display crafted firework effects or propel a player gliding with elytra, depending on how it was made and used.

behavior.answer: A firework rocket is a launched firework entity. It can display crafted firework effects or propel a player gliding with elytra, depending on how it was made and used.

spawning.answer: Casting a fishing rod creates a fishing bobber connected to its user.

interactions.answer: Wait for a bite, then reel in to catch fishing loot. Reeling can also pull hooked entities; treasure fishing has additional open-water conditions.

identity.answer: A fishing hook is the cast end of a fishing rod. It waits for fishing bites and can hook certain entities when you cast and reel it.

behavior.answer: A fishing hook is the cast end of a fishing rod. It waits for fishing bites and can hook certain entities when you cast and reel it.

spawning.answer: Red foxes appear in taiga and old-growth taiga biomes; snowy foxes appear in snowy taigas and groves. Foxes can also come from breeding.

drops.answer: Foxes drop items they are still carrying. They do not drop a fox-specific hide or fur item; adults can give experience.

breeding.answer: Feed sweet berries or glow berries to two adult foxes. The resulting baby trusts the breeding player, but can still follow adult foxes, so a lead helps move it away.

taming.answer: Foxes do not tame like wolves. Breed two foxes to produce a baby that trusts you; giving food to an unrelated wild fox is not the same as taming it.

variants.answer: Foxes have red and snow (white) forms. Red foxes occur in taigas, old growth pine/spruce taigas and dappled forests; snow foxes occur in snowy taigas and groves. Breeding inherits a parent’s form.

interactions.answer: Foxes can hold items in their mouths and pick up food. A trusting fox may defend a player, but it does not behave exactly like an owned wolf.

combat.answer: Foxes normally avoid attacking players, but a trusting fox can defend a player it trusts against an attacker. Wild and trusting foxes do not have identical behavior.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Red foxes naturally occur in taigas, old growth pine and spruce taigas and dappled forests; snow foxes occur in snowy taigas and groves. Moving a fox or placing snow does not recolor it or change the actual biome.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

trust.answer: Breed two foxes with sweet berries or glow berries. The resulting baby trusts the player who bred them, but still follows nearby adults that may run away. Trust is not wolf-style taming or a command to sit. Wild baby foxes do not automatically trust you.

item_holding.answer: A fox can carry a dropped item in its mouth and prefers food over non-food items. It can eat carried food, so do not treat its mouth as permanent safe storage. Giving it a food drop can make it swap out a held non-food item.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

equipment_drops.answer: A fox drops an item it is still carrying when it dies. Food it already ate cannot be recovered as a held-item drop.

identity.answer: A fox is an animal that can carry an item in its mouth. It hunts some smaller animals and can pick up dropped items. A fox bred by players can trust them, but is not a wolf-style tamed follower.

behavior.answer: A fox is an animal that can carry an item in its mouth. It hunts some smaller animals and can pick up dropped items. A fox bred by players can trust them, but is not a wolf-style tamed follower.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

identity.answer: A red fox is the ordinary orange-red fox variant.

spawning.answer: Find red foxes in taigas, old growth pine taigas, old growth spruce taigas and dappled forests.

identity.answer: A snow fox is the white fox variant.

spawning.answer: Find snow foxes in snowy taigas and groves. Breeding foxes can inherit a parent’s form; moving an adult to snow does not recolor it.
Frogs naturally spawn in swamps and mangrove swamps. To obtain a cold frog, raise a tadpole in a cold biome.

drops.answer: Frogs have no normal item drops on death. A frog eating a small magma cube produces a froglight; killing the frog does not.

breeding.answer: Feed slimeballs to two adult frogs. One lays frogspawn in suitable water; it hatches into tadpoles. The tadpoles’ growing location determines their eventual frog variant.

variants.answer: Frogs have temperate (orange), warm (white) and cold (green) forms. A tadpole’s growth biome determines its frog form; the parents’ colors do not determine it.

interactions.answer: Frogs eat small slimes and small magma cubes. Small slimes give slimeballs; small magma cubes give froglights whose color depends on the frog variant.

taming.answer: Frog cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

froglights.answer: A temperate orange frog makes ochre froglights, a warm white frog makes pearlescent froglights, and a cold green frog makes verdant froglights. The frog must eat a small magma cube.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

hatching.answer: Frogs lay frogspawn on water after breeding. It hatches into tadpoles; it is not picked up and placed like a normal inventory egg block.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

spawn_conditions.answer: Ordinary natural spawning is in swamps and mangrove swamps. A tadpole’s growth biome determines its adult frog color; moving an adult frog does not recolor it. Spawn eggs and biome-border cases are different from normal natural habitats.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

behavior.answer: A frog is an amphibian that can eat small slimes and small magma cubes. When it eats a small magma cube it produces a froglight; the frog variant determines the light's color.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. When it eats a small magma cube it produces a froglight; the frog variant determines the light's color.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It can also breathe air.

identity.answer: A temperate frog is the orange frog variant.

spawning.answer: Find temperate frogs in ordinary swamps, or raise a tadpole in a temperate biome such as plains or forest.

variants.answer: This is the temperate, orange frog. Its growth biome sets its form.

froglights.answer: A temperate frog produces a ochre froglight when it eats a small magma cube. Froglights are produced by that interaction, not ordinary frog death loot.

identity.answer: A warm frog is the white frog variant.

spawning.answer: Find warm frogs in mangrove swamps, or raise a tadpole in a warm biome such as a desert or jungle.

variants.answer: This is the warm, white frog. Its growth biome sets its form.

froglights.answer: A warm frog produces a pearlescent froglight when it eats a small magma cube. Froglights are produced by that interaction, not ordinary frog death loot.

identity.answer: A cold frog is the green frog variant.

spawning.answer: Raise a tadpole in a cold biome such as snowy plains or a grove. Ordinary natural frog spawning is in swamps and mangrove swamps; boundary conditions can affect the resulting form.

variants.answer: This is the cold, green frog. Its growth biome sets its form.

froglights.answer: A cold frog produces a verdant froglight when it eats a small magma cube. Froglights are produced by that interaction, not ordinary frog death loot.

spawning.answer: Look in Nether wastes, soul sand valleys and basalt deltas. Ghasts can spawn at any light level.

drops.answer: Ghasts can drop ghast tears and gunpowder. A ghast killed with a player-reflected fireball can also drop the Tears music disc.

combat.answer: Ghasts launch explosive fireballs. You can hit a fireball back toward the ghast. Use cover and avoid fighting at an exposed edge above lava.

taming.answer: Ghast cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Ghast cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

variants.answer: A hostile ghast is a different mob from a happy ghast. A ghastling grows into a happy ghast, not a hostile ghast.

spawn_conditions.answer: A ghast needs a solid block beneath its spawn position and about five by five blocks of clear width with four blocks of height. A cramped tunnel will not work. Light is not the deciding restriction; the biome and large clear space matter.

experience.answer: It gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: A ghast is a large flying hostile Nether mob. It fires explosive fireballs and can drop ghast tears, which are used in brewing and crafting.

behavior.answer: A ghast is a large flying hostile Nether mob. It fires explosive fireballs and can drop ghast tears, which are used in brewing and crafting.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

spawning.answer: Look in completely dark underground water from Y=-64 to Y=30 in Bedrock, outside the deep dark.

drops.answer: Glow squid can drop 1–3 glow ink sacs, with Looting increasing applicable amounts. Glow ink sacs are different from ordinary squid ink.

breeding.answer: Glow squid cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Glow squid cannot be tamed. Transporting one does not make it an owned animal.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Glow squid have baby and adult stages. They are a different species from ordinary squid and cannot be bred with food.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check light level 0, Y=-64 through 30, water and a solid roof so the location counts as underground. Ordinary surface squid use a different spawning route. Deep dark is excluded.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult gives 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Baby squid give no death experience.

experience_baby.answer: Baby squid give no experience when killed.

identity.answer: A glow squid is a passive aquatic animal with a glowing-looking body. It drops glow ink sacs used to brighten signs and make glow item frames. It does not illuminate nearby blocks like a torch.

behavior.answer: A glow squid is a passive aquatic animal with a glowing-looking body. It drops glow ink sacs used to brighten signs and make glow item frames. It does not illuminate nearby blocks like a torch.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. It drops glow ink sacs used to brighten signs and make glow item frames. It does not illuminate nearby blocks like a torch.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It cannot breathe air normally, so keep it in water.

land.answer: It needs water to breathe normally. Keeping it out of water can cause suffocation damage.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

spawning.answer: Look on snowy slopes, jagged peaks and frozen peaks, on surfaces such as stone, gravel, packed ice and snow blocks.

drops.answer: Goats do not have a normal meat or horn death drop. A goat drops a horn when it rams a suitable solid block, not simply when killed.

breeding.answer: Feed wheat to two adult goats. There is also a rare screaming or screamer variant, and breeding can pass that trait on.

variants.answer: Goats can be ordinary or screamer goats. Screamers look the same but sound different and ram more often; a natural or ordinary-parent breeding outcome has a 2% screamer chance.

interactions.answer: A goat can lose a horn by ramming a suitable block. Avoid killing it if you want horns. An empty bucket can collect milk from an adult goat.

taming.answer: Goat cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

milking.answer: Use an empty bucket on a living adult goat to get milk. Milking does not collect a goat horn.

horns.answer: An adult goat with horns can lose one by ramming stone, coal ore, copper ore, iron ore, emerald ore, logs or packed ice. Killing it is not the horn-harvesting method. A hornless goat cannot supply another horn by being killed.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

behavior.answer: A goat is a mountain animal that jumps and sometimes rams entities. Give it space near cliffs. Certain ramming interactions can produce goat horns.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. Give it space near cliffs. Certain ramming interactions can produce goat horns.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

identity.answer: A screamer goat looks like an ordinary goat but makes different sounds and rams more often.

spawning.answer: Look among goats in snowy slopes, jagged peaks and frozen peaks, or breed goats. Screamers are a rare form, not a separate biome population.

horns.answer: Screamer goats can provide the special goat-horn sound group when they ram eligible blocks and still have a horn. Killing a goat is not the horn-harvesting method.

spawning.answer: Look in water at an ocean monument. Bedrock guardian farms use fixed spawning columns tied to the monument.

drops.answer: Guardians can drop prismarine shards, prismarine crystals or cod under their loot conditions. Bedrock does not use Java’s extra random-fish drop in the same way.

combat.answer: Guardians charge a damaging beam and can hurt attackers with their spikes. Break line of sight to interrupt the beam and use good underwater equipment.

taming.answer: Guardian cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Guardian cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Guardians and elder guardians are separate mobs; an ordinary guardian does not age into an elder guardian.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock guardians use 25 predetermined columns with water-source checks, rather than spawning anywhere across a Java-style monument volume. Removing the monument blocks alone does not remove those spawning positions. Check the column, water and obstructions.

experience.answer: It gives 10 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: A guardian is a hostile aquatic mob associated with ocean monuments. It attacks with a damaging beam and can hurt attackers with its defensive spikes.

behavior.answer: A guardian is a hostile aquatic mob associated with ocean monuments. It attacks with a damaging beam and can hurt attackers with its defensive spikes.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: Waterlog a dried ghast for about 20 minutes to obtain a ghastling, then let it grow into a happy ghast.

drops.answer: A happy ghast drops its equipped harness if it has one. Adult player or tamed-wolf kills can give experience; ghastlings do not give experience.

breeding.answer: Happy ghasts cannot be bred. Make more by rehydrating more dried ghasts.

taming.answer: Happy ghasts do not need wolf-style taming. Grow a ghastling, then equip a harness on the adult.

transport.answer: A harnessed adult happy ghast can carry up to four players. The controlling rider steers it; a ghastling cannot be harnessed or ridden.

interactions.answer: Snowballs accelerate a ghastling’s growth. Use shears to remove an adult’s harness when the interaction is available.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

equipment.answer: Equip an adult happy ghast with a harness, not a saddle. It can carry up to four players. A ghastling must grow up before serving as adult transport.

water.answer: A ghastling can breathe underwater, but an adult happy ghast cannot breathe underwater indefinitely. Baby and adult environmental rules differ.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: A baby happy ghast is called a ghastling. It grows into a happy ghast; the hostile ghast is a separate mob.

spawn_conditions.answer: Happy ghasts do not use ordinary hostile-ghast spawning. Keep a dried ghast waterlogged until it becomes a ghastling. Snowballs speed up the ghastling’s growth, but two happy ghasts do not breed.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

equipment_drops.answer: A happy ghast drops its equipped harness when killed, if it had one. An unequipped ghast does not create a harness as a random drop.

identity.answer: A happy ghast is a large friendly flying mob that players can ride with a harness. Use it for aerial transport and building work; it can carry multiple players.

behavior.answer: A happy ghast is a large friendly flying mob that players can ride with a harness. Use it for aerial transport and building work; it can carry multiple players.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Use it for aerial transport and building work; it can carry multiple players.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

identity.answer: A ghastling is the baby stage that grows into a happy ghast.

spawning.answer: Waterlog a dried ghast until it becomes a ghastling. Snowballs can help the ghastling grow; it is not an ordinary hostile ghast spawn.

transport.answer: A ghastling is not the adult flying transport. Let it grow before equipping the adult with a harness.

spawning.answer: Find hoglins in crimson forests and certain bastion areas, especially hoglin stables. Crimson-forest hoglins can respawn over time.

drops.answer: Adult hoglins can drop porkchops and leather. Burning changes porkchops to cooked porkchops. Baby hoglins do not give the adult item loot, although they can give experience.

breeding.answer: Feed crimson fungi to two adult hoglins. They cannot breed while fleeing from warped fungi, respawn anchors or Nether portals.

combat.answer: Hoglins attack and knock targets back. Warped fungi can repel them. Even babies can be aggressive.

interactions.answer: Outside the Nether, a hoglin can convert into a zoglin. A zoglin cannot be bred with crimson fungus like a living hoglin.

taming.answer: Hoglin cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

conversion.answer: A hoglin outside the Nether normally becomes a zoglin after about 15 seconds. A name tag does not prevent that dimension-based conversion.

fire.answer: Hoglins are not normally immune to fire or lava, despite living in the Nether.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Hoglins have baby and adult stages. Zombification produces a zoglin, which is a different mob rather than an ordinary growth stage.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural hoglins can spawn at any light level in crimson forests. In Bedrock, Nether wart blocks and shroomlights are unsuitable spawning surfaces. Leave adequate space; bastion-generated hoglins are a separate source.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: Both adults and babies give 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Do not apply the usual baby-animal zero-experience rule here.

experience_baby.answer: A baby gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill, just like an adult.

identity.answer: A hoglin is a hostile Nether animal found in crimson environments. It attacks at close range and can be bred with crimson fungus. Outside the Nether it can transform into a zoglin.

behavior.answer: A hoglin is a hostile Nether animal found in crimson environments. It attacks at close range and can be bred with crimson fungus. Outside the Nether it can transform into a zoglin.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 40 health points (20 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

spawning.answer: Place a crafted hopper minecart on rails.

interactions.answer: A hopper minecart collects items and can pull items from a container above it. An activator rail can disable or enable its collection; it does not work exactly like a stationary hopper.

drops.answer: Breaking a hopper minecart normally drops its item and stored contents.

identity.answer: A hopper minecart is a rail vehicle that collects items. Use it to gather dropped items and move them along tracks, often underneath farms. A powered activator rail changes its collection state.

behavior.answer: A hopper minecart is a rail vehicle that collects items. Use it to gather dropped items and move them along tracks, often underneath farms. A powered activator rail changes its collection state.

spawning.answer: Look for horses in plains and savannas, including some village stables and animal pens.

health.answer: A horse’s maximum health can range from 15 to 30 health points. Health, speed and jumping ability vary between individuals.

drops.answer: Adult horses can drop leather plus equipped saddle and horse armor. Foals have no normal item or experience drops.

taming.answer: Repeatedly mount an adult horse until it accepts you and shows hearts. A saddle is needed to control the tamed horse; putting a saddle on another animal does not tame it.

breeding.answer: Feed golden carrots or golden apples to two tamed adult horses. Breeding a horse with a tamed donkey produces a mule, which cannot breed.

transport.answer: A tamed horse can be controlled with a saddle and equipped with horse armor. Horses cannot carry chests; use a donkey or mule for storage.

variants.answer: Horses combine seven coat colors (white, creamy, chestnut, brown, black, gray and dark brown) with five marking patterns, making 35 combinations. Coat color does not specify a separate biome or guarantee speed, jump or health.

equipment.answer: Equip a tamed adult horse with a saddle to control it while riding. Horse armor is a separate equipment slot; a chest cannot turn an ordinary horse into a pack donkey.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawning.answer: Husks are desert zombie variants that normally appear on the surface, and can also come from suitable trial spawners.

drops.answer: Husks can drop rotten flesh, with rare player-kill drops such as iron ingots, carrots or potatoes. Equipment and jockey-related drops have separate conditions.

combat.answer: Husks attack up close and can give Hunger. Unlike ordinary zombies, they do not burn in sunlight.

interactions.answer: A husk kept submerged can become a regular zombie; a regular zombie can then convert into drowned. Riders and mounts are separate entities.

taming.answer: Husk cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Husk cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Husks do not burn in sunlight like ordinary zombies. They can still take other kinds of damage.

conversion.answer: A husk submerged in water can first convert into a normal zombie. Continued submersion can then turn that zombie into a drowned; it does not skip straight from husk to drowned.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

growth.answer: Baby undead of this kind do not normally grow into adults while they remain undead. A cured baby zombie villager can later grow as a living villager.

variants.answer: Husks can be babies or adults. Water conversion into a zombie is different from a baby simply growing up.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock husks naturally use desert surface spawning, replacing many ordinary zombies. A dark underground desert tunnel is not the same surface route. Monster-spawner or trial-spawner encounters should be treated separately.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points for an adult or 12 for a baby after an eligible player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add experience; items picked up later are a separate category.

experience_baby.answer: The base baby reward is 12 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add more; this is different from ordinary baby animals giving no experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

identity.answer: A husk is a desert zombie variant that does not burn in sunlight. Its attacks can inflict Hunger, so it remains dangerous even in daytime.

behavior.answer: A husk is a desert zombie variant that does not burn in sunlight. Its attacks can inflict Hunger, so it remains dangerous even in daytime.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: Find iron golems in villages, or construct one. Bedrock village spawning has bed, villager and working requirements; it does not use Java’s three-panicking-villager setup.

construction.answer: Build a T shape with four iron blocks and place a carved pumpkin or jack o’lantern on top last, leaving space for the arms and body.

drops.answer: An iron golem drops 3–5 iron ingots and 0–2 poppies. Looting does not increase those amounts.

health.answer: An iron golem has 100 health points (50 hearts) at full health. Cracks indicate damage levels, not separate maximum-health variants.

interactions.answer: Use iron ingots to repair an iron golem. Naturally spawned golems can become hostile if you attack villagers or damage village standing; a player-built golem has different targeting behavior.

taming.answer: Iron golem cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Iron golem cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults. They are created using their construction or summoning method instead.

combat.answer: Naturally spawned iron golems can attack players when provoked or when village reputation makes the player a target. Player-built golems do not normally attack their creator. They also defend against many hostile mobs.

repair.answer: Use iron ingots to repair an iron golem. Its cracked appearance shows damage; the cracks do not represent separate maximum-health variants.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

water.answer: Iron golems do not drown. They sink rather than swim like a player, but can walk along the bottom. Drowning immunity does not make them immune to lava.

fall_damage.answer: Iron golems are immune to ordinary fall damage. They are not immune to every other damage source.

variants.answer: Iron golems show cracks as their health decreases. Cracks show damage, not a different breed; iron ingots can repair them.

spawn_conditions.answer: A Bedrock village needs at least 20 beds and 10 villagers, all villagers linked to beds, and at least 75% of eligible villagers having worked recently. The village center must be in simulation distance, with a valid unobstructed spawning surface nearby. Three frightened villagers alone are not the Bedrock requirements.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: It gives no experience when killed. Item drops and rewards from other interactions are separate.

identity.answer: An iron golem is a strong guardian mob often associated with villages. It attacks many hostile mobs and can protect a settlement. Attacking villagers or golems can make some golems hostile to you.

behavior.answer: An iron golem is a strong guardian mob often associated with villages. It attacks many hostile mobs and can protect a settlement. Attacking villagers or golems can make some golems hostile to you.

spawning.answer: Lightning occurs during thunderstorms. A suitable Channeling trident hit can also produce lightning.

interactions.answer: Lightning can start fires, damage creatures and transform certain mobs: pigs into zombified piglins, villagers into witches, creepers into charged creepers, and red or brown mooshrooms into the other color.

identity.answer: A lightning bolt is a weather event that can also be summoned as an entity. It can damage entities, ignite blocks, and transform certain mobs. Lightning rods help direct nearby strikes.

behavior.answer: A lightning bolt is a weather event that can also be summoned as an entity. It can damage entities, ignite blocks, and transform certain mobs. Lightning rods help direct nearby strikes.

spawning.answer: Throw a lingering potion to create its projectile, which makes an area-effect cloud when it breaks.

interactions.answer: Lingering potions leave a temporary cloud that applies the potion’s effect to eligible entities in its area.

identity.answer: A lingering potion is a throwable potion that leaves an effect cloud. Entities entering the cloud can receive the potion's effect while the cloud lasts.

behavior.answer: A lingering potion is a throwable potion that leaves an effect cloud. Entities entering the cloud can receive the potion's effect while the cloud lasts.

spawning.answer: Look for llamas in windswept hill biomes and savanna plateaus. Bedrock also allows them in ordinary and windswept savannas.

health.answer: A llama can have 15–30 maximum health points. Storage strength and health vary between individuals.

drops.answer: Adult llamas can drop leather, plus attached chest contents and equipped carpet where applicable. Babies do not have the normal adult item drops.

taming.answer: Repeatedly mount an adult llama until it accepts you and displays hearts. A tamed llama is not steered with a saddle like a horse.

breeding.answer: Feed hay bales to two tamed adult llamas. Wheat can feed a llama but is not the breeding item.

transport.answer: Llamas can carry chests with storage determined by their strength. Lead one to form a caravan. A carpet decorates a llama; it is not a steering saddle.

variants.answer: Llamas have white, cream, gray and brown coats. Carpet color, trader decoration and chest storage are separate from the coat.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

storage.answer: A chest gives the llama storage based on its strength. Carpets decorate it but do not set its strength; llamas are not steered with a horse saddle.

equipment.answer: Llamas use carpets for decoration and chests for storage. Riding a llama does not make it steer like a saddled horse.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural llamas require grass blocks, light above 7 and eligible hills or savanna habitats. Bedrock includes regular and windswept savannas as well as savanna plateaus. Trader llamas arrive with wandering traders rather than being ordinary wild herds.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful llama breeding can give experience, but I am not sure of the exact amount. This is separate from the adult’s death reward.

equipment_drops.answer: A llama drops its equipped carpet, attached chest and stored contents when killed. These are separate from ordinary leather drops.

identity.answer: A llama is a tameable pack animal. Equip it with a chest for cargo and use a lead to guide a caravan. It can spit at targets when provoked.

behavior.answer: A llama is a tameable pack animal. Equip it with a chest for cargo and use a lead to guide a caravan. It can spit at targets when provoked.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. Equip it with a chest for cargo and use a lead to guide a caravan. It can spit at targets when provoked.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

identity.answer: This is a white llama coat.

spawning.answer: Look for llamas in suitable savanna and windswept-hill biomes. Their coat colors are not separate biome-exclusive species.

storage.answer: A llama’s strength controls its chest storage capacity; its coat color does not determine that strength.

identity.answer: This is a cream llama coat.
