spawning.answer: Llamas and trader llamas spit when attacking or defending themselves.

combat.answer: Llama spit is a ranged attack, not an item you can collect. A provoked llama or a trader llama defending its trader can spit at a target.

identity.answer: Llama spit is the projectile a llama spits at a target. It is a defensive ranged attack rather than an item you normally collect.

behavior.answer: Llama spit is the projectile a llama spits at a target. It is a defensive ranged attack rather than an item you normally collect.

spawning.answer: Find magma cubes in the Nether, especially basalt deltas, and from magma-cube spawners in bastion treasure rooms.

health.answer: Large magma cubes have 16 health points, medium cubes have 4 and small cubes have 1. Killing a larger cube can split it into smaller cubes.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream; the small size does not normally drop it. If a frog eats a small magma cube, the result is a froglight whose color depends on the frog.

combat.answer: Magma cubes damage targets on contact and can split into smaller attackers. They are resistant to fire and lava; the smallest size can still hurt you.

taming.answer: Magma cube cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Magma cube cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults. Larger ones split into smaller ones when killed; that is not food-based breeding.

powder_snow.answer: Magma cubes take extra freezing damage in powder snow even though ordinary fire and lava do not hurt them.

variants.answer: Magma cubes have small, medium and large forms. Larger cubes split into smaller ones when killed; splitting is not food-based breeding.

water.answer: It can swim, but staying submerged for 15 seconds starts drowning damage. A larger cube can split into smaller cubes when it dies. Lava immunity does not mean immunity to drowning.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural magma-cube spawning permits any light level but needs enough clear space without solid or liquid obstructions. Space is checked before the cube’s final size is selected, so a tiny gap is not sufficient just because small cubes exist. Monster spawners are a separate source.

experience.answer: Small, medium and large cubes give 1, 2 and 4 experience points respectively after a qualifying player kill. Those values are per cube killed, not a combined total for every smaller cube that might split from it.

identity.answer: A magma cube is a bouncing hostile Nether mob. Larger cubes split into smaller ones when killed. Their drops are used for magma cream and related recipes.

behavior.answer: A magma cube is a bouncing hostile Nether mob. Larger cubes split into smaller ones when killed. Their drops are used for magma cream and related recipes.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: It is fire-immune, so sunlight does not make it take ordinary burning damage.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

identity.answer: This is the small magma cube size.

health.answer: This size has 1 health points.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream. Small magma cubes do not have the ordinary magma-cream drop; a frog eating a small one makes a froglight.

identity.answer: This is the medium magma cube size.

health.answer: This size has 4 health points.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream. Small magma cubes do not have the ordinary magma-cream drop; a frog eating a small one makes a froglight.

identity.answer: This is the large magma cube size.

health.answer: This size has 16 health points.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream. Small magma cubes do not have the ordinary magma-cream drop; a frog eating a small one makes a froglight.

spawning.answer: Place a minecart item on rails.

transport.answer: Minecarts move along rails and can carry a rider. Powered rails provide propulsion when powered; ordinary rails do not supply continuous power.

drops.answer: Breaking a minecart normally drops its minecart item.

identity.answer: A minecart is a rail vehicle for transporting entities. Place it on rails and use powered track or other mechanisms to move riders along a route.

behavior.answer: A minecart is a rail vehicle for transporting entities. Place it on rails and use powered track or other mechanisms to move riders along a route.

spawning.answer: Red mooshrooms naturally spawn on mycelium in mushroom fields. Brown mooshrooms come from special transformations or rare breeding outcomes rather than ordinary natural spawning.

drops.answer: Adult mooshrooms have cow-like leather and beef drops. Shearing is different: it gives mushrooms and turns the mooshroom into a cow.

breeding.answer: Feed wheat to two adult mooshrooms. They cannot breed with ordinary cows. Same-color parents have a rare chance to produce the opposite-color variant.

variants.answer: Red mooshrooms spawn naturally in mushroom fields. Brown mooshrooms come from lightning conversion or a rare breeding mutation; a red/brown pair can produce either color.

interactions.answer: Use a bucket for milk or a bowl for mushroom stew. A brown mooshroom fed a suitable flower gives suspicious stew on the next bowl interaction. Shearing permanently converts it into a cow.

taming.answer: Mooshroom cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

lightning.answer: Lightning swaps a mooshroom between red and brown. It does not always turn every struck mooshroom brown; an already-brown one turns red.

shearing.answer: Shearing an adult mooshroom gives five matching mushrooms and converts it into a cow. The mushrooms do not grow back on that cow.

milking.answer: Use a bucket for milk or a bowl for mushroom stew. A brown mooshroom fed a suitable small flower gives the corresponding suspicious stew on the next bowl milking; red mooshrooms do not.

conversion.answer: Shearing turns a mooshroom into a cow. Lightning instead switches its red/brown form. Those two interactions do not have the same result.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural red mooshrooms require mushroom fields and mycelium. Brown mooshrooms do not naturally spawn: use lightning conversion or the rare opposite-color offspring from breeding two matching mooshrooms. Ordinary cows and red mushrooms do not combine into a mooshroom.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

spawning.answer: Obtain a mule by breeding a horse with a donkey. Mules do not naturally spawn in a biome.

health.answer: A mule’s maximum health can range from 15 to 30 health points.

drops.answer: Adult mules can drop leather, plus an equipped saddle, attached chest and stored contents. Babies have no normal item or experience drops.

taming.answer: Repeatedly mount an adult mule until it accepts you and shows hearts. Equip a saddle to control it.

breeding.answer: Mules cannot breed. Produce another mule by breeding a tamed horse and a tamed donkey with golden carrots or golden apples.

transport.answer: A tamed, saddled mule can carry a chest. It cannot wear horse armor.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

storage.answer: A tamed donkey or mule can be equipped with a chest to carry inventory. Its storage chest and riding saddle are separate pieces of equipment.

equipment.answer: Use a saddle on the tamed animal to control riding, and optionally a chest for storage. It does not use ordinary horse armor.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Mules have baby and adult stages. They come from breeding a horse with a donkey and cannot breed themselves.

spawn_conditions.answer: Breed a horse and donkey rather than waiting for a wild mule. Mules cannot breed with each other.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

spawning.answer: Look in ocean biomes between Y=38 and Y=58, usually in small groups.

drops.answer: A nautilus can rarely drop a nautilus shell under the appropriate player or tamed-wolf kill conditions. Equipped saddle and nautilus armor also drop.

taming.answer: Feed pufferfish or a bucket of pufferfish to a nautilus. Each feeding may tame it, so bring more than one.

breeding.answer: At full health, suitable adult nautiluses can breed when fed fish or buckets of fish. Feeding a hurt one heals it first.

transport.answer: Equip a tamed adult nautilus with a saddle to ride it underwater. Nautilus armor provides additional protection; a ridden nautilus has its own underwater-breathing interaction.

combat.answer: Untamed adult nautiluses can retaliate with a dash when provoked and attack pufferfish. Tamed and baby nautiluses are normally passive. Stay clear of the dash path even if another creature is the target.

equipment.answer: A tamed adult uses a saddle for riding and can wear nautilus armor. Treat its rider and mount as separate entities if it originally spawned with a drowned.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Nautiluses have baby and adult stages and can be wild or tamed. A zombie nautilus is a separate undead mob.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural nautiluses need ocean water in the Y=38–58 range. A shallow river is not their natural habitat. Zombie nautiluses use a separate drowned-jockey route.

leashing.answer: You can attach a lead while it is not angry. If it becomes angry while already leashed, that alone does not break the lead, but you cannot reattach one while it remains angry. Leashing does not tame it.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

equipment_drops.answer: A nautilus drops its equipped saddle and nautilus armor when killed, if it had them. It does not generate armor merely because you used Looting.

identity.answer: A nautilus is an aquatic animal that can become a rideable mount. Tame and equip a suitable adult to travel underwater; keep it in appropriate water conditions.

behavior.answer: A nautilus is an aquatic animal that can become a rideable mount. Tame and equip a suitable adult to travel underwater; keep it in appropriate water conditions.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It cannot breathe air normally, so keep it in water.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

interactions.answer: World creators configure NPC dialogue and actions. They are different from villagers and do not use normal villager trading or breeding.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

drops.answer: Ocelots have no normal item drop. Adults can give experience when killed by a player or tamed wolf.

breeding.answer: Feed raw cod or raw salmon to two trusting adult ocelots. In Bedrock the baby trusts the player.

taming.answer: Ocelots gain trust from raw cod or raw salmon, but no longer turn into pet cats. Trust is not the same as owning a tamed cat.

interactions.answer: Approach slowly with raw fish. A trusting ocelot stops fleeing from you, and ocelots help scare creepers.

health.answer: Ocelots have 10 health points (5 hearts). Trusting an ocelot does not turn it into a tamed cat or give it a separate tamed-cat health value.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

variants.answer: Baby and adult ocelots can become trusting, but a trusting ocelot does not turn into a pet cat. Cats are a separate mob.

trust.answer: Approach carefully with raw cod or raw salmon and feed it until hearts appear. A trusting ocelot stops fleeing, but does not turn into a pet cat or gain a wolf-style sit command. In Bedrock, a baby bred from trusting ocelots trusts the player.

spawning.answer: Ominous trial spawners create these temporary entities above players or trial mobs during an ominous trial.

interactions.answer: An ominous item spawner displays an item, then releases a projectile or potion. Watch overhead during ominous trials; this is a hazard mechanism, not an ordinary loot chest.

spawning.answer: Look in jungles, especially bamboo jungles. Pandas naturally appear on grass blocks rather than podzol.

health.answer: Most pandas have 20 health points (10 hearts); weak pandas have 10 health points (5 hearts).

drops.answer: Adult pandas can drop bamboo. Baby pandas can sometimes produce slimeballs when sneezing; that is not a normal death drop.

breeding.answer: Feed bamboo to two adult pandas with at least eight bamboo plants within five blocks of each panda. In Bedrock, too little nearby planted bamboo makes them eat rather than enter love mode.

variants.answer: Panda personalities are normal, lazy, worried, playful, aggressive, weak and brown. Genetics determine the form; weak pandas have reduced health, and brown is a recessive appearance.

interactions.answer: Pandas eat bamboo and cake. Baby pandas can sneeze, sometimes producing slimeballs. Different personalities change behavior; do not treat every panda as the same temperament.

taming.answer: Panda cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

combat.answer: Adult pandas can retaliate when hit, and their personality affects their reactions. Baby pandas are passive; do not assume every adult panda behaves like a passive farm animal.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

breeding_conditions.answer: In Bedrock, each panda needs at least eight bamboo plants within five blocks to enter love mode. Feeding bamboo without enough planted bamboo nearby can make it sit and eat instead of breeding.

behavior.answer: It has no special personality action.

spawning.answer: Parched are desert skeleton variants that appear on the surface and can ride as passengers in camel-husk jockeys.

drops.answer: Parched can drop bones, arrows and, under suitable kill conditions, an arrow of weakness. Their carried equipment has separate drop rules.

combat.answer: Parched shoot arrows that can inflict Weakness. Unlike ordinary skeletons, they tolerate desert sunlight.

taming.answer: Parched cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Parched cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Parched do not burn in sunlight like ordinary skeletons. Sunlight immunity is not the same as fire or lava immunity.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: A parched is a distinct desert skeleton-type mob, not a normal skeleton wearing a different coat.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock parched naturally spawn on the desert surface at night, replacing some skeletons. Riders in camel-husk or spider-jockey encounters are another route. A random underground skeleton farm is not automatically a parched farm.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can affect the total; picked-up equipment and whether the gear itself drops are separate conditions. Looting does not multiply experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

identity.answer: A parched is a hostile undead skeleton variant. It can use ranged attacks, so use cover and avoid treating it as a passive desert animal.

behavior.answer: A parched is a hostile undead skeleton variant. It can use ranged attacks, so use cover and avoid treating it as a passive desert animal.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 16 health points (8 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

drops.answer: In Bedrock, parrots drop 1–2 feathers when killed. Java’s Looting increase should not be applied to this Bedrock drop.

breeding.answer: Parrots cannot be bred, and do not have a normal baby variant.

taming.answer: Feed suitable seeds to a parrot, such as wheat, melon, pumpkin, beetroot or torchflower seeds. Cookies are poisonous and can kill it.

interactions.answer: Tamed parrots can sit on your shoulders, imitate nearby mob sounds and dance near a playing jukebox. Never feed them cookies.

variants.answer: Parrots have red, blue, green, cyan and gray forms. Their colors do not change taming food or make them breedable.

music.answer: Parrots dance near a playing jukebox. Their dance does not make them breedable or change their permanent color.

equipment.answer: A tamed parrot can sit on its owner’s shoulder. Certain movement and water conditions make it dismount; it is not equipped like a saddled horse.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

sitting.answer: As its owner, use the tamed creature to switch between sitting and standing. Sitting keeps it from normally following you; it does not grant invulnerability. Use an empty hand to avoid a food or equipment interaction instead.

shoulder.answer: Move through your tamed parrot while it is not commanded to sit, or let it fly to you, to let it perch on your shoulder. You can carry one on each shoulder. This is separate from giving it a sit command on the ground.

imitation.answer: Parrots imitate nearby monster sounds. Hearing an imitation is not proof that the monster is attacking you or that the parrot can fight it.

food_safety.answer: Do not feed a cookie to a parrot. Cookies are harmful: in Bedrock they cause Fatal Poison and can kill it after a few seconds. Use suitable seeds for taming instead.

experience.answer: It drops 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. These are experience points, not player levels.

drops.answer: A player-killed phantom can drop 0–1 phantom membranes, with Looting increasing applicable amounts.

combat.answer: Phantoms swoop down from the sky and burn in daylight. Shelter can stop their attacks, and cats repel them.

interactions.answer: Entering a bed resets the rest timer associated with phantom spawning. The doInsomnia game rule also affects whether they can spawn in Bedrock.

taming.answer: Phantom cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Phantom cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: A phantom is a hostile flying mob associated with players who have not rested. It is not bred as a baby animal.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check prolonged time without resting, open sky above the player, suitable surface spawning locations at light 7 or less, the monster cap and the doInsomnia game rule. experience.answer: It gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: A phantom is a flying hostile mob associated with players going too long without rest. Sleep or rest to avoid attracting more phantoms, and watch for diving attacks at night.

behavior.answer: A phantom is a flying hostile mob associated with players going too long without rest. Sleep or rest to avoid attracting more phantoms, and watch for diving attacks at night.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

sunlight.answer: It can burn in direct sunlight when unprotected. Shade, water and applicable armor protection can prevent that; sunlight protection does not make it immune to lava.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It can also breathe air.

spawning.answer: Pigs appear on grass in many Overworld biomes and some village animal pens. Natural climate variants depend on their spawning biome.

drops.answer: Adult pigs can drop raw porkchops, or cooked porkchops when killed while burning. An equipped saddle also drops; babies do not have normal adult loot.

breeding.answer: Feed carrots, potatoes or beetroot to two adult pigs. The baby inherits one parent’s variant.

taming.answer: Pigs are not tamed like wolves. Food attracts them, and a saddle allows riding rather than ownership.

transport.answer: Equip a pig with a saddle and hold a carrot on a stick to steer it.

interactions.answer: Lightning can transform a pig into a zombified piglin. A saddle is equipment, not a breeding or taming item.

variants.answer: Pigs have temperate, warm and cold forms. Natural spawning chooses the form from the biome; breeding inherits a parent’s form, and moving an adult does not recolor it.

lightning.answer: Lightning can turn a pig into a zombified piglin. That is different from breeding a new pig variant.

equipment.answer: A saddle allows riding and a carrot on a stick controls the pig. A carrot on a stick is not its breeding food.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural pigs use grass blocks in eligible grassy Overworld biomes. Snowy plains, meadows, mangrove swamps and pale gardens are excluded, but cherry groves can have pigs. Natural pigs are not born with saddles; equipment and breeding are separate.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

identity.answer: A pig is a passive farm animal. Raise it for porkchops or ride a saddled pig using a carrot on a stick to steer.

behavior.answer: A pig is a passive farm animal. Raise it for porkchops or ride a saddled pig using a carrot on a stick to steer.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Raise it for porkchops or ride a saddled pig using a carrot on a stick to steer.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

identity.answer: This is the temperate pig variant.

spawning.answer: Look for temperate pigs in plains, sunflower plains, forest, flower forest, birch forest, old growth birch forest, dark forest, swamp, cherry grove. Those are natural-spawning habitats; a spawn egg can choose this form in additional biomes without making those natural spawning sites.

variants.answer: Breeding inherits a parent’s variant; transporting an adult to another climate does not change its form.

identity.answer: This is the warm pig variant.

spawning.answer: Look for warm pigs in savanna, savanna plateau, windswept savanna, jungle, sparse jungle, bamboo jungle, badlands, eroded badlands, wooded badlands. Those are natural-spawning habitats; a spawn egg can choose this form in additional biomes without making those natural spawning sites.

variants.answer: Breeding inherits a parent’s variant; transporting an adult to another climate does not change its form.

identity.answer: This is the cold pig variant.

spawning.answer: Look for cold pigs in taiga, snowy taiga, old growth pine taiga, old growth spruce taiga, windswept hills, windswept gravelly hills, windswept forest, dappled forest. Those are natural-spawning habitats; a spawn egg can choose this form in additional biomes without making those natural spawning sites.

variants.answer: Breeding inherits a parent’s variant; transporting an adult to another climate does not change its form.

spawning.answer: Find piglins in Nether wastes, crimson forests and generated bastion remnants.

drops.answer: Piglin loot depends on equipment and what it was carrying. A charged-creeper kill can produce a piglin head. Bartering returns are a separate mechanic, not ordinary death loot.

trading.answer: Give an adult piglin a gold ingot and let it finish examining it to receive a random barter item. Babies accept gold but do not barter; piglin brutes do not barter. Gold nuggets and gold blocks are not substitutes for the barter ingot.

combat.answer: Wearing a piece of gold armor can prevent ordinary piglin hostility, but attacking piglins or disturbing protected containers or gold blocks can still anger them. Gold armor does not pacify piglin brutes.

interactions.answer: Outside the Nether, piglins can become zombified piglins. Adult bartering and baby item-pickup behavior are different.

taming.answer: Piglin cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Piglin cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

conversion.answer: A piglin or piglin brute outside the Nether normally turns into a zombified piglin after about 15 seconds. Gold armor does not prevent that conversion.

fire.answer: Piglins and piglin brutes are not fire-immune merely because they live in the Nether. Fire and lava can damage them.

sunlight.answer: They do not normally burn just from sunlight. The Overworld zombification timer is a different hazard.

variants.answer: Piglins can be babies or adults. A piglin brute is a separate kind of mob, not the adult stage of a baby piglin.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock natural piglins need light level 7 or less in their eligible Nether biomes. They do not naturally spawn on Nether wart blocks or magma blocks. Bastion generation is another source; ordinary piglins and piglin brutes have different replenishment rules.

anger.answer: Wearing at least one piece of gold armor can prevent ordinary piglin hostility from your appearance. It does not protect you when you attack piglins or anger them through protected-container or gold-related actions. Piglin brutes ignore that gold-armor protection.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points for an adult or 1 for a baby in Bedrock after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Equipment-related bonuses are not included in those base values.

experience_baby.answer: A baby piglin’s base reward is 1 experience point in Bedrock after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Do not use Java’s baby-piglin value of 5.

equipment_drops.answer: In Bedrock, its naturally held or worn equipment has a 25% drop chance after a player or tamed-wolf kill, plus one percentage point per Looting level, up to 28% with Looting III. The creature must actually hold or wear that item; picked-up equipment is separate.

identity.answer: A piglin is a Nether mob that can barter gold ingots for items. Wearing gold armor helps avoid ordinary piglin hostility, but certain actions still anger it. Piglin brutes do not follow the same rules.

behavior.answer: A piglin is a Nether mob that can barter gold ingots for items. Wearing gold armor helps avoid ordinary piglin hostility, but certain actions still anger it. Piglin brutes do not follow the same rules.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 16 health points (8 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Find piglin brutes in generated bastion-remnant rooms. Those original brutes do not naturally respawn.

drops.answer: Piglin brutes have a chance to drop their golden axe under suitable kill conditions, and give experience. They do not provide ordinary piglin barter loot.

trading.answer: No. Piglin brutes do not barter with gold. Use an adult ordinary piglin instead; wearing gold armor also does not make a brute friendly.

combat.answer: Piglin brutes are always hostile to players and are not pacified by gold armor. They have much more health than ordinary piglins.

taming.answer: Piglin brute cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Piglin brute cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

conversion.answer: A piglin or piglin brute outside the Nether normally turns into a zombified piglin after about 15 seconds. Gold armor does not prevent that conversion.

fire.answer: Piglins and piglin brutes are not fire-immune merely because they live in the Nether. Fire and lava can damage them.

sunlight.answer: They do not normally burn just from sunlight. The Overworld zombification timer is a different hazard.

variants.answer: Piglin brutes have no baby form. They are different from ordinary piglins and do not barter with gold.

spawn_conditions.answer: Piglin brutes are generated with bastions and do not replenish through ordinary natural spawning. Darkness, waiting or adding gold does not make a cleared bastion grow new brutes.

experience.answer: It gives 20 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

equipment_drops.answer: In Bedrock, its naturally held golden axe has a 25% drop chance after a player or tamed-wolf kill, plus one percentage point per Looting level, up to 28% with Looting III. The creature must actually hold or wear that item; picked-up equipment is separate.

identity.answer: A piglin brute is an aggressive axe-wielding mob found in bastion remnants. It does not become friendly because you wear gold and does not barter like ordinary piglins.

behavior.answer: A piglin brute is an aggressive axe-wielding mob found in bastion remnants. It does not become friendly because you wear gold and does not barter like ordinary piglins.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 50 health points (25 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Pillagers appear at pillager outposts, in patrols and during raids. Outpost spawning and patrol spawning are separate systems.

drops.answer: In Bedrock, pillagers can drop arrows and have a separate chance to drop their crossbow. Raid loot can include other items, and an eligible captain can drop an ominous bottle and banner.

combat.answer: Pillagers use crossbows and attack from range. Shielding, solid cover and separating a group can help. Do not assume Java-only disarmed-pillager tricks work in Bedrock.

interactions.answer: An ominous bottle can start the Bad Omen and Raid Omen sequence when used under the relevant conditions; killing a captain is not the same as directly starting every raid.

taming.answer: Pillager cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Pillager cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Pillagers can be patrol or raid members, and a captain carries a banner. Captain is a role, not a baby or coat variant.

spawn_conditions.answer: Pillagers have different sources: outposts, patrols and raids. Bedrock patrols can start after five and a half in-game days and use light 0–7. Bedrock outpost spawning is tied to particular positions; do not copy a Java whole-volume outpost platform without checking the Bedrock positions.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can affect the total; picked-up equipment and whether the gear itself drops are separate conditions. Looting does not multiply experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

identity.answer: A pillager is a hostile illager armed with a crossbow. It attacks from range and appears in patrols, outposts, and raids.

behavior.answer: A pillager is a hostile illager armed with a crossbow. It attacks from range and appears in patrols, outposts, and raids.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 24 health points (12 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Players enter at the world spawn or a valid personal respawn location. Beds and respawn anchors have dimension-specific rules.

drops.answer: With keepInventory off, a dying Survival player normally drops carried inventory and some experience. Creative mode and world rules change the outcome.

health.answer: A player normally has 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects and game settings can change survivability.

identity.answer: A player is a person-controlled character in the world. Players explore, build, craft, fight, and interact with the world according to their game mode and permissions.

behavior.answer: A player is a person-controlled character in the world. Players explore, build, craft, fight, and interact with the world according to their game mode and permissions.

spawning.answer: Look in snowy plains, ice spikes, frozen oceans and deep frozen oceans. Bedrock also has polar-bear spawning in some frozen rivers and snowy mountain biomes.

drops.answer: Polar bears can drop cod and salmon under their loot conditions. They do not drop fur or a hide item.

breeding.answer: Polar bears cannot be bred by players.

taming.answer: Polar bears cannot be tamed. Feeding them fish does not make them pets.

combat.answer: Adults can become hostile when a cub is nearby or when attacked. Give groups with cubs plenty of room.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: Polar bears are immune to ordinary powder-snow freezing damage. That does not make them immune to every environmental hazard.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Polar bears have cub and adult stages. An adult protecting a cub can be more dangerous than one encountered alone.

spawn_conditions.answer: Look in eligible frozen and snowy biomes rather than any place with player-placed snow. Bedrock includes additional frozen river and mountain habitats. Polar bears cannot be bred with fish, so feeding them does not create cubs.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

identity.answer: A polar bear is a large animal found in cold regions. Adults may become hostile when provoked or when a cub is threatened; it is not a tameable riding animal.

behavior.answer: A polar bear is a large animal found in cold regions. Adults may become hostile when provoked or when a cub is threatened; it is not a tameable riding animal.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

spawning.answer: In Bedrock, look in warm oceans. They are rarer there than tropical fish.

drops.answer: Pufferfish drop the pufferfish item and can also drop bones in Bedrock. Java’s bone-meal drop is a different edition rule.

breeding.answer: Pufferfish cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Pufferfish cannot be tamed. Use a water bucket to capture one.

combat.answer: Pufferfish inflate near threats and can poison nearby players. The item is also poisonous to eat; do not confuse safely collecting one with safely eating it.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Pufferfish have uninflated, partly inflated and fully inflated states. These are changing defensive states, not three different species.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock pufferfish require warm-ocean surface water, with suitable player distance around 12–32 blocks. Do not substitute Java’s lukewarm/deep-lukewarm spawning list or roof over the spawning water.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

bucketing.answer: Use a water bucket directly on the creature to capture it, then use the filled bucket to release it into suitable water. Capturing and releasing it prevents ordinary natural despawning. A dispenser can release a bucketed creature but does not capture one with a water bucket.

experience.answer: It drops 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. These are experience points, not player levels.

identity.answer: A pufferfish is an aquatic fish that inflates when threatened. Its defenses can poison nearby entities. Collect it in a bucket or use its item form in compatible brewing recipes.

behavior.answer: A pufferfish is an aquatic fish that inflates when threatened. Its defenses can poison nearby entities. Collect it in a bucket or use its item form in compatible brewing recipes.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It cannot breathe air normally, so keep it in water.

land.answer: It needs water to breathe normally. Keeping it out of water can cause suffocation damage.

spawning.answer: Rabbits appear in deserts, meadows, flower forests, taigas and several snowy biomes. Their natural fur colors depend on the biome; gold rabbits are associated with deserts and white variants with snowy areas.

drops.answer: Adult rabbits can drop rabbit hide and raw rabbit, or cooked rabbit when killed while burning. A rabbit’s foot is a separate rare player-kill drop.

breeding.answer: Feed carrots, golden carrots or dandelions to two adult rabbits. Babies usually inherit a parent’s fur, with a small chance to match the local biome.

taming.answer: Rabbits cannot be tamed as owned pets. Suitable food attracts them and can be used for breeding.

variants.answer: Natural rabbit coats are brown, black, salt, white, white splotched and gold. Gold is the desert form; white forms occur in snowy biomes. Toast is a name-tag appearance. The killer bunny is Java-only.

combat.answer: Ordinary Bedrock rabbits are passive toward players. The hostile killer bunny is a Java-only feature, not an ordinary Bedrock rabbit variant.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural rabbit coats are biome-dependent: gold in deserts, white forms in snowy habitats, and brown, black or salt forms in eligible forest/taiga/meadow habitats. Bedrock also includes frozen aquatic habitats. Spawn-egg colors do not prove natural spawning in every biome.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

identity.answer: A rabbit is a small passive animal. Breed it with suitable food and raise rabbits for hide, meat, and occasional rabbit's feet.

behavior.answer: A rabbit is a small passive animal. Breed it with suitable food and raise rabbits for hide, meat, and occasional rabbit's feet.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

identity.answer: This is the brown rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in flower forests, taigas, meadows, cherry groves and dappled forests. Do not import Java-only old-growth-taiga spawning into Bedrock.

identity.answer: This is the black rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in flower forests, taigas, meadows, cherry groves and dappled forests. Do not import Java-only old-growth-taiga spawning into Bedrock.

identity.answer: This is the salt rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in flower forests, taigas, meadows, cherry groves and dappled forests. Do not import Java-only old-growth-taiga spawning into Bedrock.

identity.answer: This is the white rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in snowy plains, ice spikes, snowy taigas, groves or snowy slopes. Bedrock also allows rabbits in snowy beaches, frozen oceans and frozen rivers.

identity.answer: This is the white splotched rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in snowy plains, ice spikes, snowy taigas, groves or snowy slopes. Bedrock also allows rabbits in snowy beaches, frozen oceans and frozen rivers.

identity.answer: This is the gold rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in deserts.

identity.answer: Toast is a named rabbit appearance.

spawning.answer: Name a rabbit Toast with a name tag. It is a naming appearance rather than a naturally spawning biome-exclusive coat.

naming.answer: Use the exact name Toast to get the special appearance. The name does not change its ordinary behavior.

identity.answer: The killer bunny is a Java-only hostile rabbit feature.

spawning.answer: The killer bunny is not an ordinary Bedrock rabbit variant and does not naturally spawn in Bedrock.

combat.answer: Normal Bedrock rabbits are passive. Do not confuse them with the Java-only killer bunny.

spawning.answer: Ravagers appear as part of raids, sometimes with an illager rider. They are not ordinary naturally spawning plains animals.

drops.answer: In Bedrock, a player-killed ravager drops a saddle. Its rider has separate loot; killing the mount does not mean every rider has died.

combat.answer: Ravagers have powerful melee attacks and a roar. A shield can help against their attack, but stay alert for the follow-up roar and any rider.

taming.answer: Ravagers cannot be tamed or ridden by a player in normal Survival.

breeding.answer: Ravager cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: A ravager may have an illager rider during a raid. The rider is a separate mob, not part of a single ravager entity.

spawn_conditions.answer: Ravagers come from raids beginning at wave three, not ordinary dark-platform spawning. Riders depend on the raid wave and difficulty. Bedrock raids do not have Java’s extra-wave system.

experience.answer: It gives 20 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

identity.answer: A ravager is a large hostile beast found in raids. It attacks with powerful close-range strikes and can damage certain plants, so keep your distance and use cover.

behavior.answer: A ravager is a large hostile beast found in raids. It attacks with powerful close-range strikes and can damage certain plants, so keep your distance and use cover.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 100 health points (50 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Salmon swim in rivers and frozen rivers, plus several ocean types. Bedrock includes ordinary and lukewarm ocean variants as well as cold and frozen oceans.

drops.answer: Salmon drop raw salmon, or cooked salmon when killed while burning. In Bedrock they can also drop bones, with the bone amount affected by the fish’s size and applicable loot conditions.

breeding.answer: Salmon cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Salmon cannot be tamed. Capture one with a water bucket to transport it.

variants.answer: Salmon have small, medium and large sizes. Their size is separate from their raw-salmon item drop.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

spawn_conditions.answer: Salmon use suitable river and ocean water, not every player-made pond. Their size variants are separate from the biome requirement. Check the water biome and surface spawning conditions rather than assuming a roofed tank will work.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

bucketing.answer: Use a water bucket directly on the creature to capture it, then use the filled bucket to release it into suitable water. Capturing and releasing it prevents ordinary natural despawning. A dispenser can release a bucketed creature but does not capture one with a water bucket.

experience.answer: It drops 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. These are experience points, not player levels.

identity.answer: A salmon is an aquatic fish found in suitable water areas. Catch it for food or collect it alive in a water bucket.

behavior.answer: A salmon is an aquatic fish found in suitable water areas. Catch it for food or collect it alive in a water bucket.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Catch it for food or collect it alive in a water bucket.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It cannot breathe air normally, so keep it in water.

land.answer: It needs water to breathe normally. Keeping it out of water can cause suffocation damage.

identity.answer: This is a small salmon.

spawning.answer: Salmon sizes can occur in the applicable river and ocean habitats; size is not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Size affects the Bedrock fish’s appearance and applicable bone quantity, not a different salmon meat item.

identity.answer: This is a medium salmon.

spawning.answer: Salmon sizes can occur in the applicable river and ocean habitats; size is not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Size affects the Bedrock fish’s appearance and applicable bone quantity, not a different salmon meat item.

identity.answer: This is a large salmon.

spawning.answer: Salmon sizes can occur in the applicable river and ocean habitats; size is not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Size affects the Bedrock fish’s appearance and applicable bone quantity, not a different salmon meat item.

spawning.answer: Sheep appear on suitable grass in many Overworld biomes and some villages. Their natural wool-color distribution depends on the climate of the spawning biome.

drops.answer: Adult sheep can drop mutton and, if not already sheared, wool matching their color. Burning changes mutton to cooked mutton. Shearing a living adult gives wool without killing it.

breeding.answer: Feed wheat to two adult sheep. Compatible parental wool colors can mix in the baby; otherwise it inherits a parent’s color.

interactions.answer: Use shears to harvest wool and dye to change its color. Sheep regrow wool by eating grass. The jeb_ name effect changes appearance, not the underlying harvested wool color.

taming.answer: Sheep cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

variants.answer: Sheep can have all sixteen wool colors. Dye changes wool color; compatible parental colors can mix when breeding. The jeb_ name cycles the appearance but does not change the underlying harvested wool color.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

shearing.answer: Use shears on an adult sheep with wool to harvest its wool without killing it. It can regrow wool by eating grass; mobGriefing and access to suitable grass can affect the process.

naming.answer: The exact name jeb_ makes the visible wool cycle through colors. It does not change the underlying wool color that shearing or death drops use.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural sheep need an eligible biome and suitable grassy spawning area. Their naturally likely wool colors vary by biome; dyeing an existing sheep is separate from natural spawning. A spawn egg can produce appearances that are not proof of wild spawning at that location.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

identity.answer: A sheep is a passive farm animal that provides wool. Use shears to collect wool, dye it to change wool color, and feed adult sheep wheat to breed them.

behavior.answer: A sheep is a passive farm animal that provides wool. Use shears to collect wool, dye it to change wool color, and feed adult sheep wheat to breed them.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Use shears to collect wool, dye it to change wool color, and feed adult sheep wheat to breed them.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 8 health points (4 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

growth.answer: A baby normally grows up after about 20 minutes of active game time. Suitable feeding interactions can accelerate growth; paused or unloaded conditions can change elapsed real time.

identity.answer: This sheep has white wool.

spawning.answer: You can dye a sheep white. Natural wool colors use their own spawning distribution; not every dyed color has a natural biome-exclusive flock.

shearing.answer: Shearing gives white wool while leaving the adult sheep alive. Eating grass can regrow its wool.

identity.answer: This sheep has orange wool.

spawning.answer: You can dye a sheep orange. Natural wool colors use their own spawning distribution; not every dyed color has a natural biome-exclusive flock.

shearing.answer: Shearing gives orange wool while leaving the adult sheep alive. Eating grass can regrow its wool.

identity.answer: This sheep has magenta wool.

spawning.answer: You can dye a sheep magenta. Natural wool colors use their own spawning distribution; not every dyed color has a natural biome-exclusive flock.
